questions.q: She has been living in this city ______ 2015.
questions.e: Since is used with a fixed point in time such as 2015; for is used with a period of time.

questions.q: He is very fond ______ mangoes.
questions.e: The adjective fond takes the preposition of.

questions.q: Neither of the two boys ______ present today.
questions.e: Neither takes a singular verb, and the sentence refers to the past, so was is correct.

questions.q: He is ______ honest man.
questions.e: Honest begins with a vowel sound because the h is silent, so an is used.

questions.q: You have finished your work, ______?
questions.e: A positive statement with have takes a negative tag with the same auxiliary: haven't you?

questions.q: She sings very ______.
questions.e: An adverb is needed to modify the verb sings, so sweetly is correct.

questions.q: The train ______ before we reached the station.
questions.e: Of two past actions, the earlier one takes the past perfect, so had left.

questions.q: Please switch ______ the lights before leaving the room.
questions.e: Switch off means to turn off a light or device.

questions.q: The sun ______ in the east.
questions.e: A universal truth takes the simple present, and sun is singular, so rises.

questions.q: Rahul is the ______ of the two brothers.
questions.e: The comparative form is used when comparing two persons, so taller.

questions.q: He apologised ______ his mistake.
questions.e: Apologise takes for with the thing one is sorry about.

questions.q: Let us go for a walk, ______?
questions.e: The tag for a sentence beginning with Let us is shall we?

questions.q: Each of the students ______ a book.
questions.e: Each is singular and takes a singular verb, so has.

questions.q: He ran ______ fast that he won the race.
questions.e: So followed by an adverb and that expresses a result: so fast that.

questions.q: The meeting has been called ______ because of heavy rain.
questions.e: Call off means to cancel.

questions.q: If I ______ you, I would apologise to him.
questions.e: An unreal present condition uses the past subjunctive were with all subjects.

questions.q: Hardly had he reached home ______ it started raining.
questions.e: Hardly is followed by when, whereas no sooner is followed by than.

questions.q: One of my friends ______ settled in Canada.
questions.e: The subject is one, which is singular, so has.

questions.q: Nobody called me, ______?
questions.e: Nobody is negative in meaning, so the tag is positive; they is used for nobody.

questions.q: She is senior ______ me by two years.
questions.e: Senior, junior, superior and inferior take to, not than.

questions.q: The news of his success was ______ received by the villagers.
questions.e: An adverb is needed to modify the past participle received, so warmly.

questions.q: The thief was ______ by the police near the bus stand.
questions.e: To apprehend means to arrest.

questions.q: By next March, he ______ here for ten years.
questions.e: A period completed by a future time takes the future perfect.

questions.q: The number of applicants ______ increasing every year.
questions.e: The number of takes a singular verb; a number of takes a plural verb.

questions.q: I could not find my pen, so I am looking ______ it everywhere.
questions.e: Look for means to search for; look after means to take care of.

questions.q: Not only ______ the exam, but he also secured the first rank.
questions.e: After a fronted Not only, the auxiliary comes before the subject: did he pass.

questions.q: Neither the manager nor the employees ______ aware of the change.
questions.e: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, employees, which is plural and past.

questions.q: He insisted that the report ______ submitted by Friday.
questions.e: After verbs such as insist, the subjunctive uses the base form be.

questions.q: I am late, ______?
questions.e: The standard tag for I am is aren't I?

questions.q: The minister's ______ remarks offended many members of the community.
questions.e: Derogatory remarks are insulting and so cause offence; the other words are favourable or neutral.
